# The standard library

<!-- Generated by `node docs/gen-std.ts` from std/*.tape and compiler/types.ts. Do not edit: edit the comments in std/ and run it again. `node docs/gen-std.ts --check` (in proof/all.ts) fails when this file is stale. -->

Every program is compiled with these files before its own, so everything here is in scope without an import. Arguments are named (`until(v: raw, byte: 10)`), but the first may go without its name (`until(raw, byte: 10)`), and an argument whose value is a name of the same name may be written bare (`until(v, byte)`). `a |> f(b: 1)` is `f(<first parameter>: a, b: 1)`. A program may define a function of the same name as one here; its own wins. For the language itself see [LANGUAGE.md](../LANGUAGE.md); for a whole service, [the guide](guide.md).

The examples under a function (`> expression`, then what it gives) are run by `tape test` on every commit. Each file also has helpers that these functions call and a program does not (their comments start `Internal:`); they are in the source, std/*.tape, and not listed here.

## Common tasks

### Respond with JSON

`respond(status: …)` answers `text/plain`. `respond_as(status: …, content: Json)` answers `application/json`; then write the body with `write_json` (a record) or `write_rows` (the rows of a query). An error body is a record too.

```tape
type Item {
  Item(id: Int, name: View)
}

type Problem {
  Problem(error: View)
}

fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  match request(raw) {
    Request(method: "GET", path: "/item") -> respond_as(status: 200, content: Json)
      |> write_json(value: Item(id: 1, name: "lamp"))
    _ -> respond_as(status: 404, content: Json) |> write_json(value: Problem(error: "not_found"))
  }
}
```

Uses: [`respond_as`](#fn-respond_as), [`Content`](#type-content), [`write_json`](#builtin-write_json), [`write_rows`](#fn-write_rows), [`respond`](#fn-respond).

### Read query parameters

`Request(query)` is the raw text after `?` (`None` when there is no `?`). A query string is encoded as a form is, so `form_field(body: query, name: "limit")` reads one parameter, decoded (`+` and `%XX`). The path never holds the query.

```tape
fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  match request(raw) {
    Request(method: "GET", path: "/items", query) -> respond(status: 200)
      |> append(view: "limit \(limit_of(query))")
    _ -> respond(status: 404)
  }
}

// ?limit=N, 1 to 100; 20 when it is absent or not a number
fn limit_of(query: Option[View]) -> Int {
  let Some(value: q) = query else -> 20
  match form_field(body: q, name: "limit") {
    Some(value: decimal(n)) if n >= 1 and n <= 100 -> n
    _ -> 20
  }
}
```

Uses: [`Request`](#type-request), [`form_field`](#fn-form_field), [`decimal`](#fn-decimal).

### Parse an integer, and route on one in the path

`decimal(v)` is `Some(n)` for canonical digits (no sign, no leading zero, at most 16 digits). Any function that returns an Option is a pattern, so `"/items/" ++ decimal(id)` routes and parses at once, and a refined type checks the range: `decimal(Id(id))`. `parse_int(text)` takes a number as people write one (a sign, leading zeros). `decimal_text(value)` and holes (`"\(n)"`) go the other way.

```tape
type Id = Int where self >= 1 and self <= 9007199254740991

fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  match request(raw) {
    Request(method: "GET", path: "/items/" ++ decimal(Id(id))) -> respond(status: 200)
      |> append(view: "item \(id)")
    Request(method: "GET", path: "/items/" ++ _) -> respond(status: 400) |> append(view: "bad id")
    _ -> respond(status: 404)
  }
}
```

Uses: [`decimal`](#fn-decimal), [`parse_int`](#fn-parse_int), [`decimal_text`](#fn-decimal_text).

### Decode a JSON body, with a 400 that says why

`decode(json: body, as: T)` is `Ok(value)` or `Err(error)`, where `error` names the field and what is wrong. Refined types validate while decoding; an `Option` field may be absent. Go on with `let Ok(…) = … else { … }`.

```tape
type Name = View where len(self) >= 1 and len(self) <= 80
type Qty = Int where self >= 1 and self <= 1000

type NewItem {
  NewItem(name: Name, qty: Qty, note: Option[View])
}

type Problem {
  Problem(error: View)
}

fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  match request(raw) {
    Request(method: "POST", path: "/items", body) -> created(body)
    _ -> respond(status: 404)
  }
}

fn created(body: View) -> Buf {
  let Ok(value: NewItem(name, qty)) = decode(json: body, as: NewItem) else {
    Err(error) -> respond_as(status: 400, content: Json) |> write_json(value: Problem(error))
  }
  respond(status: 201) |> append(view: "\(qty) of \(name)")
}
```

Uses: [`decode`](#builtin-decode), [`Result`](#type-result).

### Build a JSON list

`write_json` writes a `List` as an array, on its own or as a field, and `decode(json:, as: List[Item])` reads one back. For items computed from others, `map` them into a record type and write that. `write_rows(rows: sql_all(…))` writes the rows of a query as an array.

```tape
type Item {
  Item(name: View, qty: Int)
}

type Line {
  Line(name: View, double: Int)
}

fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  match request(raw) {
    Request(method: "POST", body) -> counted(items: decode(json: body, as: List[Item]))
    _ -> respond_as(status: 200, content: Json)
      |> write_json(value: map(list: stock(), by: fn(i: Item) -> Line { Line(name: i.name, double: 2 * i.qty) }))
  }
}

fn counted(items: Result[List[Item], View]) -> Buf {
  match items {
    Ok(value) -> respond(status: 200) |> append(view: "\(length(list: value)) items")
    Err(error) -> respond(status: 400) |> append(view: error)
  }
}

// A list is built with Cons and Nil, in a function that says its type (a `let` cannot tell which List a Nil is: C21).
fn stock() -> List[Item] {
  Cons(head: Item(name: "lamp", qty: 2), tail: Cons(head: Item(name: "desk", qty: 1), tail: Nil))
}
```

Uses: [`write_rows`](#fn-write_rows), [`write_json`](#builtin-write_json), [`List`](#type-list), [`map`](#fn-map).

### Money, exactly

Money is a `Dec[2]`: `12.30` is one, `price * qty` is exact, and a hole or `write_json` writes it with its two digits (JSON as text, `"12.30"`; decode takes a number or text, exactly). What loses a digit names its rounding, once: `mul` for a rate, `div` for a share. In the database a Dec is its count, an INTEGER (12.30 is 1230). A measurement is a Float instead (`1.5f`).

```tape
// three at the price in the query, with tax at 8.875% rounded once to the cent, half away from zero
fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  let Some(value: price) = parse_dec(text: query_of(raw), scale: 2) else -> respond(status: 400)
  let net = price * 3
  let tax = mul(a: net, by: 0.08875, scale: 2, rounding: HalfUp)
  let each = div(a: net + tax, by: 3, scale: 2, rounding: Down)
  respond(status: 200) |> append(view: "\(net) + \(tax) = \(net + tax), \(each) each")
}

fn query_of(raw: View) -> View {
  match request(raw) {
    Request(query: Some(value: q)) -> q
    _ -> ""
  }
}
```

Uses: [`parse_dec`](#builtin-parse_dec), [`mul`](#builtin-mul), [`div`](#builtin-div), [`Rounding`](#type-rounding).

### Validate characters

`v[i]` is the byte at `i`, as an Int. `is_digit`, `is_lower`, `is_upper`, `is_alpha`, `is_alnum`, `is_space` and `is_hex` test one byte; `every_byte(v: …, keep: …)` is True when `keep` holds for every byte of `v`, and `keep` may be a function of your own.

```tape
// a slug: 1 to 32 bytes of a-z, 0-9 and -; decode's 400 for one that is not says the text after else
type Slug = View where len(self) >= 1 and len(self) <= 32 and every_byte(v: self, keep: slug_byte) else "1 to 32 of a-z, 0-9 and -"

fn slug_byte(b: Int) -> Bool {
  is_lower(b) or is_digit(b) or b == 45
}

fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  match request(raw) {
    Request(method: "GET", path: "/s/" ++ Slug(s)) -> respond(status: 200) |> append(view: s)
    _ -> respond(status: 400)
  }
}
```

Uses: [`every_byte`](#fn-every_byte), [`is_lower`](#fn-is_lower), [`is_digit`](#fn-is_digit), [`is_alpha`](#fn-is_alpha), [`is_alnum`](#fn-is_alnum), [`len`](#builtin-len).

### Read a request header, set a response header

`header_of(request: r, name: "if-none-match")` is the header's value, `None` when it was not sent (the service passes accept, content-type, if-match, if-none-match, idempotency-key and x-…, never cookie or authorization). `header(name:, value:)` adds one to an answer, before or after the body; the content type is `respond_as`'s.

```tape
fn handle(raw: View) -> Buf {
  let r = request(raw)
  match r {
    Request(method: "GET", path: "/old") -> respond(status: 301) |> header(name: "location", value: "/new")
    Request(method: "GET", path: "/new") -> match header_of(request: r, name: "if-none-match") {
      Some(value: "v1") -> respond(status: 304)
      _ -> respond(status: 200) |> header(name: "etag", value: "v1") |> append(view: "new")
    }
    _ -> respond(status: 404)
  }
}
```

Uses: [`header_of`](#fn-header_of), [`header`](#fn-header), [`Request`](#type-request).

## Built-ins

Provided by the compiler itself. A built-in that needs a capability (`Sql`, `Remote`, `Clock`, `Entropy`, `Timer`) uses the one the entry point declares (`fn handle(raw: View, db: Sql, clock: Clock)`), by name, without passing it.

### builtin len

```tape
len(v: View) -> Int
```

The number of bytes in a View. (A Buf: `size`.)

### builtin slice

```tape
slice(v: View, from: Int, to: Int) -> View
```

The bytes from `from` up to, not including, `to`; no copy. `v[i]` is one byte, as an Int.

### builtin buf

```tape
buf() -> Buf
```

A new, empty buffer to write into. A response starts as one: `respond`.

### builtin wrapping_add

```tape
wrapping_add(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
```

a + b modulo 2^64: the low 64 bits of the exact result. Plain `+` traps on overflow (trap 6); use this where wrapping is meant (a hash).

### builtin wrapping_sub

```tape
wrapping_sub(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
```

a - b modulo 2^64: the low 64 bits of the exact result. Plain `-` traps on overflow (trap 6); use this where wrapping is meant (a hash).

### builtin wrapping_mul

```tape
wrapping_mul(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int
```

a * b modulo 2^64: the low 64 bits of the exact result. Plain `*` traps on overflow (trap 6); use this where wrapping is meant (a hash).

### builtin float

```tape
float(n: Int) -> Float, float(n: Dec[s]) -> Float
```

The Float nearest `n`, a tie to the even one: exact up to 2^53 for an Int. The one way from an Int or a Dec to a Float; there is no implicit conversion.

### builtin dec

```tape
dec(n: Int, scale: s) -> Dec[s]
```

The Int as a Dec[s], exactly: `dec(n: 3, scale: 2)` is 3.00. Beyond the Decs it traps (integer overflow, trap 6). The scale is a number written in the call.

### builtin rescale

```tape
rescale(x: Dec[s], to: t) -> Dec[t]
```

The same number with more digits after the point, exactly (t ≥ s): `rescale(x: 1.5, to: 3)` is 1.500. Fewer digits is `round`. Traps (trap 6) when it does not fit.

### builtin round

```tape
round(x: Dec[s], to: t, rounding: Rounding) -> Dec[t]
```

The nearest Dec with fewer digits (t < s), as the rounding says: `round(x: 2.345, to: 2, rounding: HalfEven)` is 2.34.

### builtin to_int

```tape
to_int(x: Dec[s], rounding: Rounding) -> Int
```

The Int a Dec rounds to: `to_int(x: -2.5, rounding: HalfEven)` is -2, with `Floor` -3.

### builtin mul

```tape
mul(a: Dec[s], by: Dec[u], scale: t, rounding: Rounding) -> Dec[t]
```

The exact product, rounded once to t digits: `a * b` is a Dec[s + u], and this is for when that has more digits than you keep, or more than 18. The product is 128 bits, so it traps (trap 6) only when the result does not fit. `by` may be an Int.

### builtin div

```tape
div(a: Dec[s], by: Dec[u], scale: t, rounding: Rounding) -> Dec[t]
```

The quotient at t digits, rounded once: `div(a: 1.00, by: 3.00, scale: 2, rounding: HalfEven)` is 0.33. Exact in between (128 bits), so `a * b / c` loses nothing before the one rounding. By zero it traps (trap 4). `by` may be an Int. A Dec has no `/`.

### builtin parse_dec

```tape
parse_dec(text: View, scale: s) -> Option[Dec[s]]
```

The Dec[s] the text is, exactly: JSON's number syntax (`12.30`, `-0.5`, `1.23e1`), with no more digits after the point than s unless they are zeros (`12.300` is 12.30, `12.345` is None for a Dec[2]). No sign `+`, no spaces, no leading zeros.

### builtin write_dec

```tape
write_dec(out: Buf, value: Dec[s]) -> Buf
```

Appends a Dec with exactly its scale's digits after the point: `12.30`, `-0.05`, `0.00` (what a hole, `"\(x)"`, writes).

### builtin to_dec

```tape
to_dec(x: Float, scale: t, rounding: Rounding) -> Dec[t]
```

The Float's exact value (a binary fraction) rounded to t digits: `to_dec(x: 2.675f, scale: 2, rounding: HalfUp)` is 2.67, as 2.675f is a little below 2.675.

### builtin trunc

```tape
trunc(x: Float) -> Int
```

The Int toward zero: the one way from a Float to an Int (`floor` or `ceil` first for the other ways). Outside the Ints (beyond ±9.2e18) it traps, integer overflow (trap 6).

### builtin floor

```tape
floor(x: Float) -> Float
```

The integer below or equal, as a Float (`floor(-0.5f)` is -1).

### builtin ceil

```tape
ceil(x: Float) -> Float
```

The integer above or equal, as a Float.

### builtin sqrt

```tape
sqrt(x: Float) -> Float
```

The square root, correctly rounded; below 0 it traps (trap 8, float not finite).

### builtin sin

```tape
sin(x: Float) -> Float
```

The sine, x in radians. musl's, in Wasm: the same bits everywhere, within 1 ulp.

### builtin cos

```tape
cos(x: Float) -> Float
```

The cosine, x in radians. musl's, in Wasm: the same bits everywhere, within 1 ulp.

### builtin exp

```tape
exp(x: Float) -> Float
```

e to the x; beyond about 709.78 it traps (trap 8, float not finite). musl's, in Wasm: the same bits everywhere, within 1 ulp.

### builtin log

```tape
log(x: Float) -> Float
```

The natural logarithm; of 0 or less it traps (trap 8). musl's, in Wasm: the same bits everywhere, within 1 ulp.

### builtin atan2

```tape
atan2(y: Float, x: Float) -> Float
```

The angle of the point (x, y), from -pi to pi; `atan2(y: t, x: 1f)` is the arctangent of t. musl's, in Wasm: within 1.5 ulp.

### builtin pow

```tape
pow(x: Float, y: Float) -> Float
```

x to the y. A negative x takes only an integer y, and a result beyond the largest Float traps (trap 8). musl's, in Wasm: within 1 ulp.

### builtin abs

```tape
abs(x: Int) -> Int, abs(x: Dec[s]) -> Dec[s], abs(x: Float) -> Float
```

The absolute value. Of the least Int (or Dec) it traps (integer overflow, trap 6).

### builtin min

```tape
min(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int, min(a: Dec[s], b: Dec[s]) -> Dec[s], min(a: Float, b: Float) -> Float
```

The smaller of two Ints, two Decs of one scale, or two Floats.

### builtin max

```tape
max(a: Int, b: Int) -> Int, max(a: Dec[s], b: Dec[s]) -> Dec[s], max(a: Float, b: Float) -> Float
```

The larger of two Ints, two Decs of one scale, or two Floats.

### builtin write_float

```tape
write_float(out: Buf, value: Float) -> Buf
```

Appends the shortest digits that read back as the Float: `0.1`, `1e+21`, `5` (what a hole, `"\(x)"`, writes).

### builtin parse_float

```tape
parse_float(text: View) -> Option[Float]
```

The Float nearest the decimal number `text` (`"0.1"`, `"-2.5e3"`), correctly rounded, the same everywhere; `None` when it is not finite (`"1e400"`) or `text` is not a decimal number: a sign, digits with or without a point (`".5"`, `"1."`), an exponent, and nothing else, so `""`, `" 1"`, `"0x10"` and `"Infinity"` are None. decode reads a Float field with it.

### builtin scan_plain

```tape
scan_plain(v: View, at: Int) -> Int
```

The first position at or after `at` whose byte is below 32, 128 or more, a quote (34) or a backslash (92); `len(v)` when there is none. Reads 16 bytes at a time (Wasm SIMD); std/json.tape finds the plain runs of a string with it. `at` outside 0 to `len(v)` traps (trap 3).

### builtin push

```tape
push(buf: Buf, byte: Int) -> Buf
```

Appends one byte.

### builtin append

```tape
append(buf: Buf, view: View) -> Buf
```

Appends text.

### builtin freeze

```tape
freeze(buf: Buf) -> View
```

The bytes written so far, as a View.

### builtin size

```tape
size(buf: Buf) -> Int
```

The number of bytes written so far.

### builtin write_json

```tape
write_json(out: Buf, value: T) -> Buf
```

Appends a value as JSON, exactly the form `decode` reads back: a record as an object, its fields by name (`Int`, `Float` (the shortest digits that read back as it), `Bool`, `View` and refinements of them, records, `List[…]` of these, `Option[…]` of one); an `Option` field that is `None` has no key, and `Some(value)` is its value; a type with several constructors as `{"Constructor": {…}}` (`{"AlwaysUp": {}}` for one without fields); a `List` as an array; `Int`, `Bool`, `View` as themselves. Refused (C09): what cannot be JSON (a `Buf`, a function, `Option` inside a `List`).

### builtin decode

```tape
decode(json: View, as: T) -> Result[T, View]
```

Reads a JSON object into the record type `T`, or an array into `List[T]` (`as: List[Item]`). Of a type with several constructors it takes the one the object's only key names, `{"Sets": {…}}`, as `write_json` writes it; else the one that has all its fields among the keys and names the most of them. A key no field names is left unread: clients send more than a service reads. A missing key, a null, a wrong kind or a refinement that fails is `Err` with the path to it: `items[2].price: missing`, `key: null`, `qty: expected an integer`, `key: expected Key, 1 to 64 bytes`, `slug: not a valid Slug` (LANGUAGE.md section 6). An `Option` field that is absent or `null` is `None`. The bytes are read in the module, once (std/json.tape); a number is read exactly from its text.

### builtin next

```tape
next(rows: Rows[T]) -> Step[T]
```

One step through the rows of `sql_all`: `Next(value, rest)` or `End`.

### builtin sql_first

```tape
sql_first(row: T, query: "… WHERE id = :id", id) -> Option[T]
```

Needs `Sql`. The first row the query returns, as `T` (its fields name the columns). Each `:name` in the query takes the argument of that name: `id` when a value of that name is at hand, `id: 7` otherwise. On a write it also takes `repeat: True`, for a write meant to apply again on each run: a count in SQL (`n = n + 1`) or an INSERT with no unique key (C54, C55; C88 refuses it where the write is safe without it); and `no_floor: True`, for a column it takes from that has no floor (C73).

### builtin sql_all

```tape
sql_all(row: T, query: "…", …) -> Rows[T]
```

Needs `Sql`. Every row, to walk with `next` or write with `write_rows`. On a write it also takes `repeat: True`, for a write meant to apply again on each run: a count in SQL (`n = n + 1`) or an INSERT with no unique key (C54, C55; C88 refuses it where the write is safe without it); and `no_floor: True`, for a column it takes from that has no floor (C73).

### builtin sql_exec

```tape
sql_exec(query: "…", …) -> Int
```

Needs `Sql`. Runs a write; the number of rows it changed. On a write it also takes `repeat: True`, for a write meant to apply again on each run: a count in SQL (`n = n + 1`) or an INSERT with no unique key (C54, C55; C88 refuses it where the write is safe without it); and `no_floor: True`, for a column it takes from that has no floor (C73).

### builtin sql_move

```tape
sql_move(row: T, query: "UPDATE … WHERE … RETURNING *", …) -> Move[T]
```

Needs `Sql`. A compare-and-set: `Moved(value)`, `Raced(now)` when the row was not in the state the WHERE names, `NoRow`. On a write it also takes `repeat: True`, for a write meant to apply again on each run: a count in SQL (`n = n + 1`) or an INSERT with no unique key (C54, C55; C88 refuses it where the write is safe without it); and `no_floor: True`, for a column it takes from that has no floor (C73).

### builtin call

```tape
call(to: Remote, method: "…", send: Msg, reply: Reply, within: Int, once: Key) -> Result[Reply, CallError]
```

Needs `Remote`. A command to another program's `export fn`. The same `once` key runs at most once and gets the stored reply.

### builtin ask

```tape
ask(to: Remote, method: "…", send: Msg, reply: Reply, within: Int) -> Result[Reply, CallError]
```

Needs `Remote`. A read from another program: `call` without a key.

### builtin remote

```tape
remote(of: Remotes, index: Int) -> Remote
```

Needs `Remotes`. One member of a family of Remotes: `remote(of: shards, index: fnv1a(v: key) % count)`.

### builtin now

```tape
now() -> Int
```

Needs `Clock`. Milliseconds since 1970, in the log so a replay sees it.

### builtin random

```tape
random() -> Int
```

Needs `Entropy`. 53 random bits, in the log.

### builtin wake

```tape
wake(after: Int, key: Int) -> Int
```

Needs `Timer`. Asks the host to run the program's `export fn woken(…, message: Wake)` with `Wake(key)` after `after` ms. Setting a key again moves its time. Run it with `do wake(…)`.

### builtin rollback

```tape
rollback(out: Buf) -> Buf
```

Answers `out` and undoes this request's writes since its last call.

## std/core.tape

The types and functions the compiler itself refers to.

### type Option

```tape
type Option[T] {
  Some(value: T)
  None
}
```

A value that may be absent: Some(value) or None. `let Some(value: x) = e else -> fallback` goes on with x.

### type Move

```tape
type Move[T] {
  Moved(value: T)
  Raced(now: T)
  NoRow
}
```

What a compare-and-set did (sql_move). Moved: the row was in the state the statement compares, and is now as its RETURNING says. Raced: the row is there but was not in that state (another request moved it first); `now` is the row as it is. NoRow: there is no such row.

### type Result

```tape
type Result[T, E] {
  Ok(value: T)
  Err(error: E)
}
```

A value or the reason there is none. Errors are values: match on them, or go on with one case a step at a time, `let Ok(value: x) = e else { Err(error) -> … }`.

### type CallError

```tape
private type CallError {
  Timeout
  Unreachable
  Rejected(reason: View) final
  Skew(reason: View) final
}
```

Why a call to another object or Worker gave no reply. Timeout: the time budget ran out, and for a call that changes something the outcome is unknown until it is sent again with the same key. Unreachable: nothing answers to that name. Rejected: it refused, and says why. Skew: the two sides disagree, so nothing ran this time: they were built from different definitions of the method, or the key was used before for another message (which may have run; do not compensate for a Skew as for a refusal). Rejected and Skew are final: the callee runs a key at most once and repeats its stored reply, so the same call sent again gets the same answer; a timer that asks again does not change it (rules.ts C79 lets such an outcome leave a row for a request to move on).

### type Wake

```tape
type Wake {
  Wake(key: Int)
}
```

What the host sends to `export fn woken` when a timer set with wake(timer, after, key) is due: that key.

### type Rounding

```tape
type Rounding {
  HalfEven
  HalfUp
  Down
  Up
  Floor
  Ceiling
}
```

How a Dec loses digits (round, to_int, mul, div, to_dec): HalfEven sends a tie to the even neighbour (2.5 to 2, -2.5 to -2), HalfUp sends it away from zero (2.5 to 3, -0.5 to -1); Down goes toward zero, Up away from it, Floor toward minus infinity and Ceiling toward plus infinity. The compiler reads the constructors in this order.

### type Step

```tape
type Step[T] {
  Next(value: T, rest: Rows[T])
  End
}
```

One step through the rows of a query: next(rows) gives Next(value, rest) or End.

### fn same

```tape
fn same(a: View, b: View) -> Bool
```

Text equality, used by == on View and by text patterns.

```
> same(a: "lamp", b: "lamp")
True
> "lamp" == "lamps"
False
```

### fn find_text

```tape
fn find_text(v: View, sep: View, at: Int) -> Int
```

Where sep first occurs in v, at or after at; -1 when it does not. Used by text patterns `p ++ "sep" ++ q`.

```
> find_text(v: "/runs/12/advance", sep: "/", at: 1)
5
> find_text(v: "abc", sep: "x", at: 0)
-1
```

### fn concat

```tape
fn concat(a: View, b: View) -> View
```

Text joined: `a ++ b` in an expression is concat(a, b). (In a pattern, `"prefix" ++ rest` takes text apart.)

```
> "Hello, " ++ "ada" ++ "!"
"Hello, ada!"
> concat(a: "", b: "")
""
```

## std/text.tape

Bytes and text.

### fn until

```tape
fn until(v: View, byte: Int) -> View
```

The part of v before the first `byte`, or all of v when it has none.

```
> until(v: "key=value", byte: 61)
"key"
> "no equals sign" |> until(byte: 61)
"no equals sign"
```

### fn after

```tape
fn after(v: View, byte: Int) -> View
```

The part of v after the first `byte`, or nothing when it has none.

```
> after(v: "key=value", byte: 61)
"value"
> after(v: "key", byte: 61)
""
```

### fn find

```tape
fn find(v: View, byte: Int, at: Int) -> Int
```

The position of the first `byte` at or after `at`, or len(v).

### fn starts_with

```tape
fn starts_with(v: View, prefix: View) -> Bool
```

Does v begin with `prefix`?

```
> starts_with(v: "/todos/7", prefix: "/todos/")
True
> "/todo" |> starts_with(prefix: "/todos/")
False
```

### fn has

```tape
fn has(v: View, at: Int, word: View) -> Bool
```

Is `word` at position `at` of v?

### fn is_digit

```tape
fn is_digit(b: Int) -> Bool
```

Is the byte an ASCII digit, 0-9?

```
> is_digit(b: 55)
True
> is_digit(b: 97)
False
```

### fn is_lower

```tape
fn is_lower(b: Int) -> Bool
```

Is the byte an ASCII lower-case letter, a-z?

```
> is_lower(b: "a"[0])
True
```

### fn is_upper

```tape
fn is_upper(b: Int) -> Bool
```

Is the byte an ASCII upper-case letter, A-Z?

```
> is_upper(b: "a"[0])
False
```

### fn is_alpha

```tape
fn is_alpha(b: Int) -> Bool
```

Is the byte an ASCII letter, a-z or A-Z?

```
> is_alpha(b: "_"[0])
False
```

### fn is_alnum

```tape
fn is_alnum(b: Int) -> Bool
```

Is the byte an ASCII letter or digit?

```
> is_alnum(b: "Z"[0])
True
```

### fn is_space

```tape
fn is_space(b: Int) -> Bool
```

Is the byte white space: a space, a tab, a line feed or a carriage return?

```
> is_space(b: 9)
True
```

### fn every_byte

```tape
fn every_byte(v: View, keep: Fn[Int, Bool]) -> Bool
```

Does every byte of v pass `keep`? True for "" (nothing fails). For a slug, a key or a code of a fixed alphabet:

```
> every_byte(v: "order-17", keep: fn(b: Int) -> Bool { is_lower(b) or is_digit(b) or b == 45 })
True
> every_byte(v: "Order 17", keep: is_alnum)
False
```

### fn char_count

```tape
fn char_count(v: View) -> Int
```

How many characters v holds: its code points, each UTF-8 sequence counted once, where `len` counts bytes ("é" is 2 bytes and 1 character). For a limit a spec states in characters: `type Name = View where char_count(v: self) <= 64`. Text that is not valid UTF-8 counts each byte that does not continue a sequence.

```
> char_count(v: "日本語")
3
> char_count(v: "é!")
2
```

### fn isqrt

```tape
fn isqrt(n: Int) -> Option[Int]
```

The square root of `n`, rounded down: the largest r with r * r <= n. None when n is negative. Exact for every Int, up to the largest (whose root is 3037000499). For fixed point, scale first: the root of 2 to 3 places is isqrt(2 * 1000 * 1000), 1414 thousandths.

```
> isqrt(n: 17)
Some(value: 4)
> isqrt(n: 2 * 1000 * 1000)
Some(value: 1414)
> isqrt(n: -1)
None
```

### fn digits_end

```tape
fn digits_end(v: View, at: Int) -> Int
```

The position of the first byte at or after `at` that is not a digit.

### fn decimal

```tape
fn decimal(v: View) -> Option[Int]
```

A canonical decimal number: digits only, no leading zero, at most 16 digits.

```
> decimal(v: "42")
Some(value: 42)
> decimal(v: "042")
None
> decimal(v: "12a")
None
```

### fn parse_int

```tape
fn parse_int(text: View) -> Option[Int]
```

An integer as people write one: an optional sign (`-` or `+`), then one or more digits, leading zeros and all; None for anything else, and for a number an Int cannot hold. For a value from a form, a query or a CSV field. `decimal` is the strict one, for ids in a path: no sign, no leading zero, so "/orders/007" is not order 7.

```
> parse_int(text: "007")
Some(value: 7)
> parse_int(text: "-42")
Some(value: -42)
> parse_int(text: "+5")
Some(value: 5)
> parse_int(text: "-9223372036854775808")
Some(value: -9223372036854775808)
> parse_int(text: "9223372036854775808")
None
> parse_int(text: "1.5")
None
> parse_int(text: "-")
None
```

### fn decimal_text

```tape
fn decimal_text(value: Int) -> View
```

A number in decimal, as text.

```
> decimal_text(value: 2000)
"2000"
> "attempt " ++ decimal_text(value: -3)
"attempt -3"
```

### fn write_int

```tape
fn write_int(out: Buf, value: Int) -> Buf
```

Appends a number in decimal.

```
> buf() |> append(view: "n=") |> write_int(value: -305) |> freeze
"n=-305"
```

### fn write_text

```tape
fn write_text(out: Buf, text: View) -> Buf
```

Appends text: append(buf: out, view: text) with the names write_* use.

### fn write_code

```tape
fn write_code(out: Buf, code: Int) -> Buf
```

Appends a code point as UTF-8.

### type Utf8

```tape
type Utf8 {
  Utf8(code: Int, next: Int)
  BadUtf8
}
```

One UTF-8 sequence starting at a byte >= 128 (RFC 3629: no overlong forms, no surrogates, nothing above U+10FFFF).

### fn utf8_at

```tape
fn utf8_at(v: View, at: Int) -> Utf8
```

The code point that starts at `at` (a byte of 128 or more), and where the next one starts; BadUtf8 when it is not valid UTF-8.

## std/json.tape

JSON (RFC 8259), read by stepping and written by appending.

Reading an object:   json_first(v) gives the first step, json_next(v, at) the step after a member:

```
Member(key, value, next)   one member; key is decoded; value is a Json; next is where to continue
Close(next)                the object ended at next
Malformed                  not JSON
```

Strings must be valid UTF-8 and well-formed Unicode: a lone surrogate escape is Malformed. A repeated key is reported again; the caller decides (JSON.parse keeps the last).

### type Json

```tape
type Json {
  JsonString(text: View)
  JsonBool(value: Bool)
  JsonOther
}
```

A value of a member, as json_first and json_next give it: text and booleans; anything else is JsonOther.

### type JsonStep

```tape
type JsonStep {
  Member(key: View, value: Json, next: Int)
  Close(next: Int)
  Malformed
}
```

One step through an object: a member, the end of the object, or text that is not JSON.

### fn json_first

```tape
fn json_first(v: View) -> JsonStep
```

The first step of the object that v holds (whitespace around it allowed).

### fn json_next

```tape
fn json_next(v: View, at: Int) -> JsonStep
```

The step after a member whose `next` was `at`.

### fn json_end

```tape
fn json_end(v: View, at: Int) -> Bool
```

Does only whitespace follow position `at`?

### fn json_value

```tape
fn json_value(v: View, at: Int) -> JsonValue
```

The value that starts at `at`.

### fn number_end

```tape
fn number_end(v: View, at: Int) -> Option[Int]
```

-? (0 | [1-9][0-9]*) (. [0-9]+)? ([eE] [+-]? [0-9]+)?

### fn skip

```tape
fn skip(v: View, at: Int, byte: Int) -> Int
```

at + 1 when v[at] is `byte`, else at.

### fn json_text

```tape
fn json_text(v: View, at: Int) -> JsonText
```

The string whose body starts at `at` (after the opening quote), decoded. A string without escapes is returned as a view of the input; one with escapes is decoded into new memory.

### fn is_hex

```tape
fn is_hex(b: Int) -> Bool
```

Is the byte a hex digit (0-9, a-f, A-F)?

```
> is_hex(b: 70)
True
> is_hex(b: 103)
False
```

### fn hex

```tape
fn hex(b: Int) -> Int
```

The value of a hex digit (is_hex(b) must hold).

```
> hex(b: 102)
15
```

### fn write_json_string

```tape
fn write_json_string(out: Buf, text: View) -> Buf
```

Appends text as a JSON string, escaped exactly as JSON.stringify escapes it.

```
> buf() |> write_json_string(text: "a\nb") |> freeze
"\"a\\nb\""
```

### fn write_bool

```tape
fn write_bool(out: Buf, value: Bool) -> Buf
```

Appends true or false.

```
> buf() |> write_bool(value: True) |> freeze
"true"
```

### fn json_int

```tape
fn json_int(text: View) -> Option[Int]
```

The value of a JSON number's text when it is a whole number within ±(2^53 - 1), read exactly (no rounding); None otherwise. `text` must be a JSON number (number_end found it).

```
> json_int(text: "1e3")
Some(value: 1000)
> json_int(text: "-2.50e1")
Some(value: -25)
> json_int(text: "1.5")
None
> json_int(text: "9007199254740992")
None
```

### fn write_rows

```tape
fn write_rows[T](out: Buf, rows: Rows[T]) -> Buf
```

Every row of a query as a JSON array, each row written as write_json writes it.

## std/http.tape

A request, parsed. The host passes METHOD SP TARGET LF BODY; the target is PATH or PATH?QUERY. A request that came through a published name's public route (no token: anyone) ends its line with a word, METHOD SP TARGET SP public, and `caller` is Anyone; every other request is the operator's. The request headers the host passes follow on the same line, each after a carriage return, `CR name: value`, names in lower case. `query` is None when the target has no `?`, and Some("") when it ends with one: they are different requests.

### type Caller

```tape
type Caller {
  Operator
  Anyone
}
```

Who sent a request: the operator (with the token), or Anyone, through a published name's public route.

### type Request

```tape
type Request {
  Request(method: View, path: View, query: Option[View], body: View, caller: Caller, headers: View)
}
```

A request as `request(raw)` gives it. `path` is the target before `?`, as sent (percent-encoding is not undone); `query` the raw text after `?` (read one parameter with `form_field(body: q, name: "limit")`); `body` what follows the first line feed; `headers` the request headers the host passed, read with `header_of`.

```
match request(raw) {
  Request(method: "GET", path: "/items/" ++ decimal(id)) -> …
  Request(method: "POST", path: "/items", body) -> …
}
```

### fn request

```tape
fn request(raw: View) -> Request
```

The request `handle` is given, parsed.

```
> request(raw: "POST /holds?x=1 public\nqty=1")
Request(method: "POST", path: "/holds", query: Some(value: "x=1"), body: "qty=1", caller: Anyone)
> request(raw: "GET /k/a b\n")
Request(path: "/k/a b", caller: Operator)
> request(raw: "GET /items?\n")
Request(path: "/items", query: Some(value: ""))
> request(raw: "GET /items\n")
Request(path: "/items", query: None)
> request(raw: "GET /k\raccept: text/html\n") |> header_of(name: "Accept")
Some(value: "text/html")
```

### fn header_of

```tape
fn header_of(request: Request, name: View) -> Option[View]
```

The value of a request header, by its name in any case; the first one when there are several. A host passes only the headers it means a program to see (the service: accept, content-type, if-match, if-none-match, idempotency-key and x-…, never cookie or authorization).

```
> request(raw: "POST /\rcontent-type: text/csv\ridempotency-key: 7\nbody") |> header_of(name: "Idempotency-Key")
Some(value: "7")
> request(raw: "GET /\n") |> header_of(name: "accept")
None
> request(raw: "GET /\rx-a: 1\n") |> header_of(name: "accept")
None
```

### fn lower

```tape
fn lower(text: View) -> View
```

ASCII letters in lower case; every other byte as it is.

```
> lower(text: "Content-Type")
"content-type"
```

### fn respond

```tape
fn respond(status: Int) -> Buf
```

A response: the status, a line feed, then the body written by the caller. It is served as text/plain. The status line is in the Buf, so text to keep (a body to store, a value to compare) starts from `buf()`, not from here.

```
> freeze(buf: respond(status: 200) |> append(view: "ok"))
"200\nok"
> freeze(buf: buf() |> append(view: "ok"))
"ok"
```

### fn header

```tape
fn header(out: Buf, name: View, value: View) -> Buf
```

A response header, on an answer begun by respond or respond_as: `respond(status: 302) |> header(name: "location", value: url)`. The status line carries it, after a carriage return: STATUS[ SP TYPE](CR name: value)* LF BODY. A name is 1 to 64 token characters (letters, digits, and !#$%&'*+-.^_`|~) and a value up to 4096 bytes with no CR, LF or NUL; the host refuses any other (the request is answered 500 and says why), and those it sets itself (content-type, which is respond_as's, content-length, set-cookie, the security headers…).

```
> respond(status: 302) |> header(name: "Location", value: "/links/7") |> freeze
"302\rlocation: /links/7\n"
> respond(status: 200) |> append(view: "hi") |> header(name: "cache-control", value: "no-store") |> freeze
"200\rcache-control: no-store\nhi"
```

### type Content

```tape
type Content {
  Html
  Json
  Text
  Css
  Svg
  Csv
}
```

The content types the service serves: respond_as(status: 200, content: Html) answers text/html.

### fn respond_as

```tape
fn respond_as(status: Int, content: Content) -> Buf
```

A response with a content type: the status, then the body written by the caller. respond_as(status: 200, content: Json) answers application/json; `respond` answers text/plain.

```
> respond_as(status: 201, content: Json) |> append(view: "{}") |> freeze
"201 application/json\n{}"
```

### fn content_type

```tape
fn content_type(content: Content) -> View
```

The media type a Content is served as.

```
> content_type(content: Json)
"application/json"
```

### fn form_field

```tape
fn form_field(body: View, name: View) -> Option[View]
```

One field of an application/x-www-form-urlencoded body (what an HTML form POSTs), decoded: `+` is a space and %XX a byte. None when the form has no such field; the first one when it has several.

```
> form_field(body: "qty=2&buyer=ada+l%C3%B6", name: "buyer")
Some(value: "ada lö")
> form_field(body: "qty=2", name: "buyer")
None
> form_field(body: "x=1&done", name: "done")
Some(value: "")
```

### fn write_html

```tape
fn write_html(out: Buf, text: View) -> Buf
```

Text into HTML, as text: & < > " and ' are written as entities, so a value from a request (a name, a note) cannot open a tag or end an attribute.

```
> freeze(buf: write_html(out: buf(), text: "<b>Tom & \"Jo\"</b>"))
"&lt;b&gt;Tom &amp; &quot;Jo&quot;&lt;/b&gt;"
```

## std/list.tape

An immutable list. Adding to the front shares the rest; nothing is ever changed in place.

### type List

```tape
type List[T] {
  Cons(head: T, tail: List[T])
  Nil
}
```

An immutable list: Cons(head, tail) or Nil. Build one in a function that says its type, `fn items() -> List[Item]`.

### fn length

```tape
fn length[T](list: List[T]) -> Int
```

How many items.

```
> length(list: Cons(head: 1, tail: Cons(head: 2, tail: Nil)))
2
```

### fn reverse

```tape
fn reverse[T](list: List[T]) -> List[T]
```

The same items, last first.

```
> Cons(head: 1, tail: Cons(head: 2, tail: Nil)) |> reverse
Cons(head: 2, tail: Cons(head: 1, tail: Nil))
```

### fn map

```tape
fn map[A, B](list: List[A], by: Fn[A, B]) -> List[B]
```

A new list with `by` applied to every item.

```
> Cons(head: 1, tail: Cons(head: 2, tail: Nil)) |> map(by: fn(x: Int) -> Int { x * 10 })
Cons(head: 10, tail: Cons(head: 20, tail: Nil))
```

### fn filter

```tape
fn filter[A](list: List[A], keep: Fn[A, Bool]) -> List[A]
```

The items for which `keep` is True, in the same order.

```
> Cons(head: 1, tail: Cons(head: 2, tail: Cons(head: 3, tail: Nil))) |> filter(keep: fn(x: Int) -> Bool { x % 2 == 1 })
Cons(head: 1, tail: Cons(head: 3, tail: Nil))
```

### fn fold

```tape
fn fold[A, B](list: List[A], from: B, by: Fn2[B, A, B]) -> B
```

Combine the items left to right, starting from `from`: by(by(from, first), second) and so on. `from` may be a Buf, handed from item to item, to write each item into it.

```
> Cons(head: 3, tail: Cons(head: 4, tail: Nil)) |> fold(from: 100, by: fn(acc: Int, x: Int) -> Int { acc - x })
93
> Cons(head: 1, tail: Cons(head: 2, tail: Nil)) |> fold(from: buf(), by: fn(out: Buf, n: Int) -> Buf { out |> write_int(value: n * 10) }) |> freeze
"1020"
```

### fn range

```tape
fn range(from: Int, to: Int) -> List[Int]
```

The Ints from `from` up to `to`, not `to` itself: none when `to` is not above `from`. Folded, it is a counting loop: `fold(list: range(from:, to:), …)` never makes the list, and takes a step a number, as over a list of that length (compiler/fuse.ts).

```
> range(from: -1, to: 2)
Cons(head: -1, tail: Cons(head: 0, tail: Cons(head: 1, tail: Nil)))
> range(from: 1, to: 5) |> fold(from: 0, by: fn(acc: Int, n: Int) -> Int { acc + n })
10
```

### fn join

```tape
fn join(list: List[View], sep: View) -> View
```

The texts with `sep` between each two.

```
> join(list: Cons(head: "a", tail: Cons(head: "b", tail: Cons(head: "c", tail: Nil))), sep: ", ")
"a, b, c"
> join(list: Nil, sep: ", ")
""
```

## std/map.tape

An immutable map from text to any value, kept in key order (an AVL tree). `put` returns a new map that shares all but one path with the old one; the old map is unchanged. Walk it in order by matching on Node(left, key, value, right) and Empty.

### type Map

```tape
type Map[V] {
  Node(left: Map[V], key: View, value: V, right: Map[V], height: Int)
  Empty
}
```

A map from text keys to values of type V. Start from Empty; put and get.

### fn before

```tape
fn before(a: View, b: View) -> Bool
```

Does a sort before b, byte by byte?

### fn compare

```tape
fn compare(a: View, b: View) -> Int
```

Where a sorts against b, byte by byte: -1 before it, 0 the same text, 1 after it. A text sorts before every longer text it starts.

```
> compare(a: "desk", b: "lamp")
-1
> compare(a: "lamp", b: "lam")
1
> compare(a: "rug", b: "rug")
0
```

### fn get

```tape
fn get[V](map: Map[V], key: View) -> Option[V]
```

The value under `key`, if there is one. One comparison of the keys at each node.

```
> Empty |> put(key: "lamp", value: 3) |> put(key: "desk", value: 1) |> get(key: "lamp")
Some(value: 3)
> Empty |> put(key: "lamp", value: 3) |> get(key: "rug")
None
```

### fn put

```tape
fn put[V](map: Map[V], key: View, value: V) -> Map[V]
```

A map with `key` set to `value`; the old map is unchanged. Setting a key again replaces its value. One comparison of the keys at each node.

```
> Empty |> put(key: "a", value: 1) |> put(key: "a", value: 2) |> get(key: "a")
Some(value: 2)
```

### fn put_with

```tape
fn put_with[V](map: Map[V], key: View, from: V, by: Fn[V, V]) -> Map[V]
```

A map with the value under `key` replaced by `by` of it, or set to `by(from)` when the key is not there: one walk down the tree where get and then put take two, and a path whose heights did not change is not balanced again. Counting words is `put_with(map: counts, key: word, from: 0, by: plus_one)`.

```
> Empty |> put_with(key: "a", from: 0, by: fn(n: Int) -> Int { n + 1 }) |> put_with(key: "a", from: 0, by: fn(n: Int) -> Int { n + 1 }) |> get(key: "a")
Some(value: 2)
> Empty |> put_with(key: "a", from: 10, by: fn(n: Int) -> Int { n * 2 }) |> get(key: "a")
Some(value: 20)
```

### fn count

```tape
fn count[V](map: Map[V]) -> Int
```

How many keys.

```
> Empty |> put(key: "a", value: 1) |> put(key: "b", value: 2) |> put(key: "a", value: 3) |> count
2
```

## std/retry.tape

When to try again, as a library on top of one capability. backoff is pure arithmetic; retry_later also sets a timer (wake, which needs Timer), so the host calls the program's `woken` with Wake(key) when the time comes. Nothing here is syntax, and a program that never calls it sets no timers.

### type Backoff

```tape
type Backoff {
  Backoff(first: Int, factor: Int, most: Int, tries: Int)
}
```

How long to wait after each failure in a row: `first` ms after the first, `factor` times longer after each one after that, never longer than `most` ms; and how many attempts in all, the first one included.

### type Retry

```tape
type Retry {
  RetryIn(after: Int, attempt: Int)
  GaveUp(tries: Int) final
}
```

What to do after a failure: try again in `after` ms (that will be attempt number `attempt`), or stop, because all `tries` attempts have failed. GaveUp is final: backoff gives it again for as many failures or more, so a row a program gives up on waits for a request (C79).

### fn backoff

```tape
fn backoff(policy: Backoff, failed: Int) -> Retry
```

After `failed` failures in a row (1 after the first), what to do. The same answer every time.

```
> backoff(policy: Backoff(first: 1000, factor: 2, most: 30000, tries: 5), failed: 1)
RetryIn(after: 1000, attempt: 2)
> backoff(policy: Backoff(first: 1000, factor: 2, most: 30000, tries: 5), failed: 3)
RetryIn(after: 4000, attempt: 4)
> backoff(policy: Backoff(first: 1000, factor: 3, most: 5000, tries: 9), failed: 4)
RetryIn(after: 5000, attempt: 5)
> backoff(policy: Backoff(first: 1000, factor: 2, most: 30000, tries: 5), failed: 5)
GaveUp(tries: 5)
```

### fn grown

```tape
fn grown(wait: Int, factor: Int, most: Int, times: Int) -> Int
```

`wait`, `times` times multiplied by `factor`, stopping once it reaches `most`.

```
> grown(wait: 10, factor: 2, most: 1000, times: 3)
80
```

### fn capped

```tape
fn capped(wait: Int, most: Int) -> Int
```

The smaller of the two: a wait never longer than `most`.

```
> capped(wait: 7000, most: 5000)
5000
```

### fn retry_later

```tape
fn retry_later(timer: Timer, key: Int, policy: Backoff, failed: Int) -> Retry
```

backoff, and when it says to try again, a timer for then: `woken` gets Wake(key) that many ms from now. The key names what to retry (an order's id, say); setting it again moves its time, so a key is retried once.
